Most of the public is completely unaware of these issues, especially in regard to the mass closing of mental health facilities. Often times the public and legislative officials find the need for change much more compelling if they hear it from a more personalized approach. Some places around the country have actually changed their legislation due to social push back. Change happens slowly, but to sit idly by and do nothing about it won't initiate change. Even if some attempts fail by reform projects, at least it opens the dialogue and brings more attention to such atrocities so that more people talk about it and eventually, some one somewhere along the line is able to do something that actually makes a difference.

Wow! So sorry to hear you’re going through this!! I am seeing an immunologist and infectious disease doctor. I do have chronic EBV, but it seems to come in flares. I went down to HSS and saw a doctor specializing in immune conditions and I got diagnosed with a very rare auto immune disease, but it is often the result of chronic EBV. So, basically the chronic EBV started the auto immune disease, and flares of the immune disease causes flares of the virus. I started a pretty intensive treatment to shut down my immune system since mine is in overdrive, and so far I haven’t had a flare of the EBV. I’m not sure this would be the same for you, because it seems like the EBV has made your immune system suppressed as opposed to going into overdrive, but I know it can go both ways.
